title: Ridge-Spin-Layer Coupling and Emergent Ridgetronics in 2D Altermagnets
authors: Mu Tian, Run-Wu Zhang, Chaoxi Cui, Zhi-Ming Yu, Yugui Yao
abstract: Extending valleytronics from discrete points to continuous lines in momentum space transforms dispersionless bands into a controllable degree of freedom. Here we introduce ridge--spin--layer coupling (RSLC) in two-dimensional (2D) altermagnets, where a one-dimensional continuous line of dispersionless electronic states (a ridge) in momentum space locks to both spin polarization and atomic sublayer. This ridge-induced quenching of kinetic energy mimics flat-band physics, yet crucially, RSLC grants external control, allowing for layer-selective switching of ridge orientation in reciprocal space, spin-filtered transport in real space, and a distinct electric Hall response. Guided by collinear spin layer group symmetry, we identify three 2D candidate materials, namely Mg$_2$Mo$_2$(PO$_5$)$_2$, Ca(FeP)$_2$, and Mg$_2$V$_2$(SO$_5$)$_2$, each featuring a crossed-ridge structure with two ridges, one per spin channel and sublayer. Our work establishes ridgetronics as a controllable platform for direction-discriminating currents, bridging dispersionless bands with multifunctional device operation.
summary: This paper introduces 'ridgetronics,' a novel platform for electrical control over charge transport in 2D altermagnets. It achieves this by exploiting Ridge-Spin-Layer Coupling (RSLC), which locks electronic states into continuous, dispersionless lines in momentum space. The resulting material properties allow for highly directional, spin-polarized currents and electric field-tunable Hall effects.
main_problem: The research aims to extend valleytronics by developing 'ridgetronics,' which controls directional current flow using continuous lines of electronic states in momentum space.
main_result: Ridge-Spin-Layer Coupling (RSLC) is established in 2D altermagnets, allowing electric field control over spin-filtered transport and inducing an Electric Hall Effect.
method: The work uses symmetry group theory to derive conditions for ridge states and employs tight-binding models combined with band structure calculations.
model_or_system: The system is based on 2D altermagnets on a square lattice, featuring continuous lines of dispersionless electronic states (ridges) coupled to spin polarization and atomic sublayers. The Hamiltonian describes this coupling using specific orbital hopping terms.
key_observables: Direction-discriminating currents, layer-selective switching via electric field ($E_z$), spin-polarized conductivities ($\sigma_{xx}, \sigma_{yy}$), and the Electric Hall Response ($\sigma_{xy}$).
important_parameters: The coupling strength (RSLC) is crucial; the system must be altermagnetic with specific symmetry operations $\{C_2||O_L\}$ connecting orthogonal ridges.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a 2D square lattice structure and relies on the existence of specific spin-layer group symmetries to support the coupling mechanism.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transition from discrete valleys to continuous ridges, show band structures derived from tight-binding models for candidate materials like Mg2Mo2(PO5)2, and demonstrate layer-dependent Q1D spin transport and EHE effects.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the concept of ridgetronics via RSLC in altermagnets. It then uses symmetry analysis to identify suitable candidate materials ($	ext{Mg}_2	ext{Mo}_2(	ext{PO}_5)_2$, etc.). Finally, it details how electric fields control spin-polarized transport and induce novel electrical responses.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state magnetism, the concept of controlling electronic states via symmetry constraints (Spin Layer Group Theory) and achieving highly directional, tunable current flow echoes principles used in designing quantum devices where coupling between multiple degrees of freedom is key.
